pairs.subject: error-handling
pairs.evidence: crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:70 The contract's CommandError carries only a closed code plus the Rust error's Display text, so the refusal reason (typed Refusal/RefusalCode in table_app::Error) crosses the IPC boundary as prose, and the client recovers it by regex-stripping 'mandate clause N: ' and looking the remaining text up in a word table (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/mandateDraft.ts:302); the taxonomy also has no catch-all or transience axis.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:70 Code survives the boundary, but category-specific data (the refusal reason) is flattened to Display text. The far side then classifies prose: refusalWords() regex-strips the message and looks it up, which is the stringification-at-a-boundary bug the technique names.

crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:32 Closed and small (8 members) with a stable spelling, but it has no explicit unknown/catch-all member and no transient-vs-permanent axis. table_app::Error::Ledger(_) falls through to LedgerTrust as the default branch (lib.rs:66). The TS side folds unrecognised failures into UNAVAILABLE.

crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:56 There is no internal class. DomainError (InvalidTransition, Json decode of stored data, InvalidTerms) and ProtocolError are folded into Invalid, a user-input class. Impossible states then read as the caller's fault, and the zero-rate detector is lost.

crates/table-client/src/run_state.rs:27 Cancelled is correctly kept apart from Failed, but RunSnapshot carries it as a bare name with no cause. Owner pause, quit_confirm and actor shutdown (table-runtime dispatcher.rs:774/782, actor.rs:639) all produce the same causeless value on the wire.

crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:31 Across the published Rust-to-TS boundary, the failure is a closed enum with a stable serialized spelling, exported via ts-rs (generate-bindings.rs:18) and drift-tested. That is the shape the technique prescribes for a cross-boundary consumer.
crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:393 The contract publishes a typed wallet:error event, so background runtime faults have a defined door to the UI rather than dying in the runtime.
crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:256 The only decode in the context reads a single owner-picked file, where the item is the whole input. This crate reads no externally-owned collection item by item.
crates/table-client/src/bin/generate-bindings.rs:2 The only binary is a build-time bindings generator whose callers branch only on zero vs non-zero, so there is no multi-code exit contract.
crates/table-client/src/lib.rs:1 This is a DTO/contract library with no process or execution-context edge of its own. Last-resort handlers belong to the shell and runtime contexts.

pairs.registryProposal: consumer-decides-error-shape and taxonomy-design say the category must cross a published boundary as a value. They do not say that category-specific payload (here a typed refusal reason) must too. A contract can have a perfectly closed code enum while a sub-reason travels only in the message, forcing the far side into prose matching. Consider stating that any sub-classification a consumer branches on is part of the published enumeration, not of the message.
